subject: PrivDeploy: CI traffic simulation & IaC contract validation
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Cc: security@acme.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: PrivDeploy: CI traffic simulation & IaC contract validation

Hi all,

Following up from last week's sync — Acme is gearing up for a private deployment and asked us to validate that our Terraform/Helm/Ansible module contracts hold under realistic CI traffic patterns and safety guardrails (esp. prefix/KV cache behavior, egress rules, and bastion jump workflows). I want to run a short, repeatable simulation inside a staging environment that mimics:

- CI burst: many short-lived connections (concurrent jobs)
- Long-lived sessions: persistent inference traffic to exercise KV cache and routing fallbacks
- Egress-constrained environment: simulate restricted internet access + proxying through customer NAT

Goals: confirm modules tolerate bursts without queueing > SLO, verify helm values don't cause pod restarts under layered config, and ensure Ansible post-provision steps (bastion + creds roll) don't break in constrained networks.

Attached: draft simulation plan, TF module compatibility matrix, and a k6 load script skeleton. Can you review the plan and call out any missing failure modes or gating checks? Marissa — can ops run the sim in the priv-staging cluster next week? Karthik — any concerns about pins/versions or deterministic infra teardown? Jenna — quick note on Acme constraints would be great so we can bake them into the simulation.

Thanks,
Soojin
--
Soojin Lee
Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachments: priv-ci-traffic-simulation-plan.md (text/markdown), tf-module-compat-matrix.csv (text/csv), k6-load-script.js (application/javascript)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>

Subject: Re: PrivDeploy: CI traffic simulation & IaC contract validation

Thanks, Soojin — this looks like the right surface. A few notes from the infra side:

- Terraform: we should exercise both module variants we offer (v1.3.x and the newer v2.0-beta). There are subtle lifecycle differences around alb/target-group nullability that can cause rollforward drift during repeated apply/destroy cycles. I've added a column in the TF matrix where we mark the drift-prone resources.

- Helm: pinning strategy matters — using imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent in staging hides flakiness. For the sim, force imagePullPolicy: Always to surface image churn. Also test chart overlays where customer values override operator defaults (we should include a small overlay that toggles kv_cache.enabled).

- Ansible: the bastion choreography currently relies on ephemeral keys from the provisioning pipeline. We need a teardown step that revokes keys, otherwise repeated runs will pollute known_hosts and cause intermittent ssh failures.

- Traffic sim: k6 is fine; suggest synthesizing two profiles: steady-state token-per-second and bursty-job-surge. Make sure to exercise prefix cache invalidation by alternating different prompt prefixes.

I'll attach a short checklist and a terraform helper script snippet to rotate module versions between runs. I'm happy to pair with Marissa during the run.

Karthik

Thanks, Soojin and team. Acme is definitely interested. A couple of constraints from our side:

- The environment will be air-gapped for the initial rollout — everything must be staged via our internal artifact repo. No outbound internet allowed except to the customer-managed proxy.
- Egress: only specific endpoints will be allowed (metrics -> prometheus.acme.internal, pkg repos -> artifactory.acme.internal).
- Maintenance windows: we can provide a 2-hour window on Aug 25 (PST) and an overnight window Aug 27-28 if needed.

We appreciate the simulation. Please ensure the teardown fully revokes ephemeral creds and that any test artifacts are destroyed. Security will want a short report showing no creds leaked and a list of APIs the sim touched.

Looking forward — Jenna

I can take the ops lead for the run on Aug 25 in Acme's 2-hour window. Action items I propose:

- Pre-run checklist (to be run by ops):
  - Confirm staging cluster snapshot taken and stored on Acme artifactory (RFID in Drive link).
  - Verify imagePull settings and ensure all images are present in internal repo.
  - Confirm NAT/proxy rules allow testing endpoints only.
  - Confirm bastion key revocation playbook is staged and dry-run passes.

- Run plan:
  1) Bring up TF modules with v1.3.x 
  2) Apply helm overlays (kv_cache.enabled toggled)
  3) Start k6 steady-state profile for 20 minutes
  4) Trigger burst profile for 5 minutes and observe evictions/restarts
  5) Run teardown and revocation scripts

I'll coordinate with Karthik on the module-rotation helper. After the run I'll produce a short postmortem and a security checklist that Jenna can review.

Marissa
